advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make test_ac5_route_selection_has_zero_early_effects drive the real short-circuit/filter path (e.g. invoke create_one with a filtered/tombstoned/read-only mutation through the coordinator route) and assert zero provider create/search calls, instead of gating the composition behind a hardcoded `short_circuited = True`.
evidence: `short_circuited = True  # stands in for filter/tombstone/read-only guards upstream`
`if not short_circuited:  # pragma: no cover - the guard holds in this scenario`
`assert provider == {"create": 0, "search": 0}` — provider was initialized to exactly this on the prior line and never mutated because the composition branch is dead

Docstring claims 'A short-circuited create (filter / read-only / tombstone) that never reaches the coordinated composition issues ZERO provider calls' but no short-circuit guard is invoked; the create_one/upstream filter path is never driven
advisory.finding: test_ac5_route_selection_has_zero_early_effects is a vacuous/regression-blind test: it hardcodes `short_circuited = True`, so the coordinated-composition branch (guarded by `if not short_circuited:` and marked `pragma: no cover`) never executes; the closing `assert provider == {"create": 0, "search": 0}` merely re-asserts the dict literal it was just initialized to. It exercises no upstream short-circuit/filter/tombstone guard (none exists in this diff) and would pass unchanged even if route consultation eagerly created — so it cannot detect a regression in the 'zero early effects' behavior it documents.
scenarios: A future regression where consulting the create route (or an upstream guard failing to short-circuit) triggers an eager create/search would leave this test green.
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace the hardcoded `short_circuited` flag with the actual upstream guard under test (route a filtered/tombstoned create through create_one/apply_outbound) so the coordinated seams would run if the guard failed, then assert provider create/search counts remain zero.
